title: Feature Request: Option to sync Keyboard Backlight with Night Color (Sunset/Sunrise)
line: Power Management settings have a new "Turn off during the day" option that switches the keyboard backlight off in the morning and back on in the evening.
explanation: Powerdevil had no link between the keyboard backlight and the time of day, so users with a backlit keyboard had to switch it on every evening and off every morning by hand. Each power profile now has a "Turn off during the day" checkbox under the keyboard brightness row. When it is on, the keyboard brightness action follows the shared day-night schedule (KNightTime, the same one Night Light, the day-night wallpaper and automatic theme switching use): it switches the backlight off at sunrise and restores the previous level (or the profile's keyboard brightness) at sunset, switching halfway through each transition like automatic theme switching does.

commits.message:
actions/keyboardbrightness: add an option to turn it off during the day

The keyboard backlight could not follow the time of day, so it had to
be switched on every evening and off every morning. A new profile option
turns it off in the morning and back on in the evening, by the schedule.

BUG: 520799

media.caption: Power Management settings on master: no way to tie the keyboard backlight to the time of day
New "Turn off during the day" option under keyboard brightness
Daytime on master: keyboard backlight stays at 100%
Daytime with the option on: powerdevil turned the keyboard backlight off (0%)
At sunset the backlight is switched back on at its previous level (100%)

review.text: Adding a per-profile "Turn off during the day" option in PowerDevil driven by KNightTime is the right design and repo placement for this feature request. However, the C++ implementation has several real bugs: KDarkLightScheduleProvider::poll() ignores its returned future and races with m_scheduleProvider and rapid profile reloads, sunset restoration forces brightness to at least 1 even when the profile explicitly sets keyboard brightness to 0% (and reads the disabled slider's stale value instead of a 50% fallback), updateDayNight() runs before applyProfileBrightness() and defeats its conservative-profile check, and the day/night QTimer uses CoarseTimer with qint64-to-int narrowing.
changes: Use the KDarkLightSchedule returned by KDarkLightScheduleProvider::poll() (or await m_scheduleProvider's initial schedule cleanly) and guard against stale callbacks if onProfileUnload/onProfileLoad occurs before the async call finishes, avoiding races with scheduleChanged.

Respect an explicit 0% profile keyboard brightness at sunset instead of clamping with std::max(value, 1), and when UseProfileSpecificKeyboardBrightness is unchecked and m_brightnessBeforeDay == 0, fall back to a fixed 50% (matching the documented behavior) rather than reading the disabled slider's stale keyboardBrightness() setting.

Order profile-load brightness application so applyProfileBrightness()'s conservative-profile check is not bypassed by updateDayNight() raising brightness from 0 first (and avoid duplicate setBrightness calls at night).

Configure m_dayNightTimer with Qt::VeryCoarseTimer (or PreciseTimer) instead of default CoarseTimer (which can drift by ~36 minutes over 12 hours), and avoid qint64-to-int overflow when nextSwitch is far away (e.g. polar latitudes).
On resumeFromSuspend, avoid restoring m_lastKeyboardBrightness before checking daytime state so the backlight does not briefly flash on (or race async setBrightness) when waking during the day.

reviews.text: Adds a per-profile 'Turn off during the day' checkbox under keyboard brightness. The keyboard brightness action then follows the shared KNightTime day/night schedule, the one Night Light and automatic theme switching use and which the reporter asked to hook into: off at the morning breakpoint, back to the previous level (or the profile level) at the evening one. The code is sound: KNightTime is already a powerdevil dependency, the schedule is polled before the first decision, the timer is re-armed on schedule changes, clock skew and resume (the existing resume restore runs first, then updateDayNight turns it off again if it is now day), and the provider is torn down on profile unload. Manual changes between transitions are respected. The settings screenshot and dbusmock UPower runs show the backlight going 3→0 by day and back by evening. The option is per profile like every other powerdevil setting, which is expected.
